motion: I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Department of Building and Safety (LADBS), in coordination with the Department of Public Works, Fire Department, Police Department, Housing Department, City Attorney and the Mayor's Office, to develop and report within 30 days on a Citywide Vacant and Public Nuisance Property Abatement Program to identify, prioritize, secure, clean, repair, demolish, or otherwise abate vacant and nuisance properties that pose significant threats to public safety and quality of life. I FURTHER MOVE that the City Council instruct LADBS, to report within 30 days on the • number, location, and status of priority vacant and public nuisance properties citywide, including properties that are vacant, unsecured, abandoned, fire-damaged, substantially deteriorated, littered with trash or debris, or associated with inactive construction, and establish criteria for prioritizing properties based on public safety risk, duration of nuisance conditions, surrounding community impacts, and other appropriate factors. Data should be sorted by Council Districts, and the report should contain protocols and timelines of opening a vacant building abatement case and the steps that follow. I FURTHER MOVE that the City Council instruct LADBS to report within 30 days on the enforcement and abatement actions available for identified priority properties, including the status of any proceedings before the Board of Building and Safety Commissioners, opportunities to expedite cases presenting significant or ongoing risks to surrounding communities, and recommendations to strengthen coordination among LADBS, the Board, the City Attorney, the Mayor's Office, and Council District Offices; I FURTHER MOVE that the City Council instruct LADBS, with assistance from the City Administrative Officer, to identify within 30 days available and potential funding sources, including the Demolition and Repair Fund and the funding contemplated in Council File No. 26-0600-S3, to support the cleanup, securing, repair, demolition, and abatement of priority nuisance properties, and report on available mechanisms to recover eligible costs from responsible property owners, including liens, penalties, and other legally available enforcement tools; and that LADBS report on recommendations for establishing an ongoing, citywide process to proactively identify and address priority vacant and nuisance properties before nuisance conditions become prolonged public safety hazards. PRESENTED BY: /ADRIN NAZARIAN , Councilmember, 2nd District SECONDED BY; __ (vnKo
title: Citywide Vacant and Public Nuisance Property Abatement Program / Criteria for Prioritizing Properties / Potential Funding Sources
